relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with a GFAP variant diagnosed with Alexander disease: "the patient was diagnosed with juvenile AxD combined with WD".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and copied supplementary-table row segments (Supplementary Table 1) from the file, checked against the table. In scope: the patient (case-report proband, label 'patient'), her father (tested: 'Her father had no variation at this locus'; diagnosed with Wilson's disease; no variant row because he does not carry the GFAP variant and the paper does not state his ATP7B genotype), and her mother (deceased, 'mental retardation since childhood'; not tested; authors say AxD could not be excluded). Including the untested mother is a judgement call. 'passed away when she was 4 years old' is ambiguous (most likely the patient's age), so the mother's age at death is left null. Variants in other genes (ATP7B x2, SLC22A5, MYH2) recorded because Supplementary Table 1 attributes them to the patient ('Identification of the patient’s genetic mutations and variants'). Supplementary Table 1 labels every variant 'Missense', including the synonymous ATP7B p.L770L and the MYH2 intronic c.T505+2C:p.? variant; variant type recorded as stated, which contradicts the HGVS. Its 'Inheritance pattern' column (AD/AR) is the disease mode, not variant origin, so inheritance is not reported. Supplementary table uses non-standard cDNA notation (c.G716C) while text gives c.716G > C; the text form is used as the original string for GFAP and ATP7B. Transcript NM_000053 for ATP7B is printed without version. GFAP inheritance left 'not reported': father negative, mother untested. Checklist: 'decreased speech' not mapped to dysarthria; academic decline not mapped to cognitive decline; 'brainstem patches' not mapped to medulla/cervical cord; 'hypotonia' and 'hypertonic tendon reflexes' both recorded as stated. Kayser-Fleischer ring, copper studies and sinus findings are Wilson's disease/incidental findings, recorded as reported. No stacked cells. No treatment reported.
